price_source: Yahoo Finance CO2.NZ regularMarketPrice, 2026-08-10 15:31 NZST, volume 4,054 units
model_type: NAV-based (net tangible assets per unit) — NOT a free-cash-flow DCF

valuation_philosophy.summary: Salt Carbon Fund is an NZX-listed unit trust whose only asset is New Zealand Units (NZUs), the compliance credits of the NZ Emissions Trading Scheme. It has no revenue, no margins, no operating cash flow and no earnings in any conventional sense — NZUs are a non-yielding commodity. A discounted-cash-flow model is therefore structurally inapplicable: there are no cash flows to discount. The fund is valued the only way such a vehicle can be: project the NZU spot price, carry NAV per unit forward at that price less the 1.0% p.a. management-fee drag, apply an exit discount to NTA reflecting the listed vehicle's persistent illiquidity, and discount back at a cost of equity.
valuation_philosophy.discount_rate_rationale: 8.5% = ~4.5% NZ risk-free + ~4.0% vehicle-specific premium for extreme illiquidity (~4,000 units/day, ~NZ$6k notional), fee drag, manager-change and wind-up/sub-scale risk. The NZU PRICE risk is deliberately NOT loaded into the discount rate — it is expressed explicitly in the bull/base/bear NZU price paths. Loading a commodity's price risk into the discount rate as well as the scenario spread double-counts it.
valuation_philosophy.key_caveat: NAV per unit tracks the NZU price roughly one-for-one, and the NZU price is set by government policy (unit supply settings, auction reserve prices, forestry and agriculture rules), not by market fundamentals. The November 2025 NDC-delinking decision cut the NZU price ~20% intraday. This valuation is a policy forecast wearing the clothes of a financial model, and should be read as such.

nav_facts.nta_source: NZX announcement — CO2's NTA as at 7/8/2026: $1.7167 (fund publishes daily NTA)
nav_facts.units_source: NZX Rule 3.13.1 buyback notice, 7 Aug 2026: 20,856,005 units in existence excluding treasury stock

treasury_units.note: The fund buys back its own units below NTA and holds them as treasury stock, having never sold any. This is mechanically NAV-accretive to remaining holders but shrinks the fund.
treasury_units.buyback_accretion_note: Recent buybacks executed at $1.54-1.5457 against NTA ~$1.72 — roughly a 10% discount, so each repurchase adds to NAV per remaining unit.

bull.rationale: ETS credibility restored: unit cap tightens, auctions clear, NZU re-rates toward the 2022 peak (~$88) and the 2026 $71 Auction Reserve Price becomes binding. Persistent sub-NAV buybacks plus renewed demand close the listed discount to ~2%.

base.rationale: NZU grinds higher on genuine private-account scarcity (stockpile down ~9.5m units YoY) but stays below the $71 auction floor as policy credibility remains only partly repaired. The structural discount narrows but does not close, because illiquidity and wind-up risk persist.

bear.rationale: Policy weakness persists or worsens (further NDC-style delinking, forestry supply, agriculture kept out). NZU re-tests the Jan-2026 ~$33 low. The fund shrinks toward sub-scale and the discount widens to 15%.

base.note: The fund pays no distributions, so there are no interim cash flows: the entry price is the base-case exit value discounted at the 15% hurdle.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.not_evaluated_reason: no rule had inputs: no annual row with revenue, equity or earnings on a known scale (core_metrics.units NULL? see make backfill-units) or no FY-end price aligned to it

risks_to_valuation: NZU price is a government policy variable — a single ETS decision can move NAV 20% in a day (Nov 2025 NDC delinking).
Extreme illiquidity: ~4,000 units/day. The quoted price can diverge from NTA in either direction for long periods, and any meaningful position cannot be exited near the quote.
The fund shrank from 47.2m to 20.9m units ex-treasury between 31 Mar and 7 Aug 2026. Continued shrinkage raises sub-scale, wind-up and delisting risk.
No distributions: total return depends entirely on exit price on a thin exchange.
1.0% p.a. fee compounds against a zero-yield asset — a certain drag regardless of NZU direction.
NZU spot of ~NZ$55 is an assumption from mid-2026 market reporting; NTA per unit is the audited-adjacent figure and should be preferred as the anchor.
